description: Seat 1 (the browser player) of the networked reconnect match. The deck exists for one reason: put an open PendingChoice in front of the reloading player on a turn that is their own, so the turn clock being asserted is the active player's clock and not R79's separate 30 s prompt clock. #65 Masochism Mask carries the Quickdraw tag (SPEC §6.2: "Starts in your opening hand instead of a draw", setup step 2), so it is in the opening hand for every seed; it costs 2, which seat 1 can pay on its second turn (§2.3: max mana = turns you have started, so 1 on player-turn 1 and 2 on player-turn 3), and its base form is "Start of turn: choose one: exile the bottom card of your library, lose 3 health, or summon a Spikey Pillow" (§8.3 #65) - one pending choice, opened for the active player at the start of their next turn. It is the only Quickdraw card here, so it replaces exactly one of the three opening draws. The other 19 cards are inert while they sit in a hand: no Cast-on-draw (#21, #27 excluded), no second Quickdraw (#84, #98 excluded), no "while in your hand" trigger (#89 excluded), no start-of-game roll, so nothing but the Mask can open a prompt or change the board before the spec asks for it. They are cheap (six cost 0 or 1) so seat 1 always has a legal play. R82 therefore does not auto-end the turn the spec means to end by clicking - at the seed this spec pins (R143 makes the room endpoint honour it under E2E=1, and rooms.test.ts proves the join uses it verbatim), which is the only claim measured. It is NOT true of every seed: a survey of 61 seeds found 14 that satisfy it, so this sentence is about the pinned seed and nothing wider.
